A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KernelBand and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The substantial algorithmic and experimental revisions can be reliably compared; differing evaluation settings limit direct performance comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original GPU kernel optimization experiments against GEAK, including performance trajectories, hardware/backend comparisons, clustering visualization, and a seeded_dropout case study.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–J report original benchmark comparisons, scaling and sensitivity experiments, component ablations, cost measurements, PyTorch comparisons, and hardware-specific strategy statistics.

M1.justification: V1's additive, learned logistic profiling bonus is replaced by hardware-saturation masks restricting UCB selection and softmax selection within clusters. V2 profiles cluster representatives rather than every candidate, changes clustering features from six dimensions to five, and replaces signed improvement rewards with nonnegative clipped rewards. These materially change the optimization procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates 29 kernels restricted to L1–L2. V2 reports 183 kernels spanning L1–L5 and 13 functional categories, with harder attention, linear-attention/SSM, quantization, and fused-operation tasks documented in Table 1 and Appendix E. This substantially broadens computational patterns and task difficulty.

E2.justification: The agent comparison expands from GEAK alone to GEAK plus Best-of-N in the main benchmark and backend experiments. Appendix G and Table 9 additionally evaluate PyTorch eager execution, torch.compile with inductor, and max-autotune as reference execution methods.

E3.justification: Default/extended budgets change from 10/20 to 20/40 iterations. V2 adds H20 and additional LLM configurations, with GPT-5 replacing the reported GPT-5.1 backend. Correctness tolerances tighten from atol=1e-3 and rtol=1e-1 to both 1e-4. Fast@1 changes from >1.1 to >1.0, shape aggregation becomes a ratio of total runtimes, and correct-only/fallback reporting modes and 50-/30-kernel subset protocols are introduced.

E4.justification: V1's clustering visualization and worked dropout case study are removed. V2 adds explicit component and framework ablations, including profiling removal and LLM strategy selection, plus clustering sensitivity over K={1,2,3,5}, cross-hardware strategy analyses, and quantitative runtime/API-cost analyses. These directly investigate mechanisms and tradeoffs that v1 largely illustrated or asserted.

E5.justification: Timing estimation changes from the mean over 1,000 timed iterations to the median over a 1,000ms measurement window; warmup likewise changes from iteration counts to duration. Appendix E newly specifies seed 42 for subset sampling. Neither version reports independent optimization-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result set is substantially replaced and expanded. For example, v1 Table 2 reports RTX 4090/DeepSeek best-of-iteration-9 speedup of 9.78× and Fast@1 of 54%; v2 Table 1 reports 1.74× and 43.3% under changed coverage, budgets, method, and metrics, so this is not a same-setting regression. V2 additionally reports correctness, ablation, strategy, cost, and PyTorch comparison outcomes.

T1.justification: V1's cluster-similarity/profiling-error regret argument is replaced by explicit hardware-gain boundedness and Lipschitz assumptions, an epsilon-optimality theorem, and an approximation/estimation decomposition in Appendix B. The bound changes from a linear cluster-strategy prefactor plus clustering/profiling errors to square-root dependence on cluster-strategy count plus a cluster-diameter approximation term. V1's asserted equivalence between cumulative reward maximization and minimum final latency is also removed.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from hierarchical UCB with learned profiling guidance to hardware-constrained contextual bandits with pruning and Lipschitz/covering-based efficiency claims. V2 foregrounds provable sample efficiency and structured selection outperforming LLM reasoning. V1's fewer-token efficiency claim is replaced by better performance per dollar, despite acknowledged higher per-iteration costs.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for preferring bandits over full reinforcement learning, budget-dependent clustering granularity, hardware-dependent strategy allocation, and profiling's larger contribution at the default budget. It also interprets raw profiling injection as potentially harmful and explains why removing the strategy set disables multiple dependent components. These substantially extend v1's clustering and dropout-based mechanism narrative.

D1.justification: Section 3.6 and Appendices A, C–H add exact profiling counters and CUDA feature APIs, code-hash caching, masking/UCB parameters, the complete six-strategy catalog, a 16,384-token output limit, the named evaluation subset, and benchmark/GEAK adaptation details. V1's logistic-training buffer, SGD, and synthetic warmup specifications disappear with the replaced component.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around profiling-based agents such as CudaForge and TritonForge, metric/clustering bandits, and hardware-aware compilation. It explicitly presents KernelBand as complementary to model fine-tuning and explains exclusions of other agents in Appendix F. V1's separate hierarchical-optimization discussion and several associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, formulation, methodology, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, the method is reorganized around characterization, clustering, and constrained selection, and the single proof appendix becomes Appendices A–J. The title, author list, and running header also change.

P2.justification: V2 introduces a system overview diagram, runtime breakdown and cost plots, and redesigned difficulty/backend comparison and ablation tables. The scalability display adds clustering configurations, while v1's separate Fast@1 trajectories, clustering scatterplot, and dropout plot disappear. New appendix tables document configurations, strategies, subsets, PyTorch results, and hardware-specific statistics.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the paper: v1's narrow easy-task evaluation and illustrative case studies give way to harder tasks, explicit component ablations, additional comparison methods, and measured cost tradeoffs. Stricter correctness checks and detailed appendices improve credibility and reproducibility. These gains outweigh losing the worked case study, although independent-run uncertainty remains absent and Appendix E's claimed <1% category deviation conflicts with Table 7. The changed protocols do not establish a direct performance improvement over v1.
